hero.title: Start with the need. Keep the solution understandable.
hero.lede: Good technical work should leave a business with clearer ownership and fewer avoidable surprises, not a system that only one person can operate.

steps.title: Assess
steps.description: Inventory the current state, clarify the outcome, identify constraints, and understand ownership, cost, privacy, security, and maintenance requirements.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Choose a proportionate architecture, work through version-controlled changes, test what matters, and avoid recurring services that exist only for convenience.

steps.title: Handoff
steps.description: Document deployment, access, recovery, rollback, and maintenance. Put business assets in the appropriate owner accounts and use named access for administration.

beforeBuild.title: A few questions usually matter more than the framework.

items.title: What outcome actually matters?
items.description: Define the business result first so the implementation does not become the goal.

items.title: What already works?
items.description: Preserve useful systems and data where practical instead of replacing everything by default.

items.title: Who should own it?
items.description: Domains, repositories, hosting, data, and administrative access should have a clear owner and recovery path.

items.title: What will it cost to keep?
items.description: Consider recurring services, maintenance effort, portability, and future change before adding infrastructure.

principles.title: Maintainable by design.
items: Secure named access and least practical privilege

handoff.title: A project should not become a dependency on the person who built it.
handoff.body: The final state should make ownership, deployment, access, maintenance, and recovery understandable. When continued support makes sense, it can be provided without turning basic ownership into a subscription requirement.
